summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: @servicetitan/carto-charts-rn@0.0.2 declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"` in package.json. On install, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases`, unzips it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run a bundled 727KB file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a Bun-CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) obfuscated with a shifted string-array dispatcher (`function WV8StW(...) {... MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())... }`), a large numeric decoder table (`const n7gIxM=[...]`), and mangled identifiers, so the code that executes on the installer cannot be audited from the shipped source. The delivery pattern — a Node preinstall hook fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute a bundled opaque payload — is unrelated to the package's stated purpose (a React Native charts wrapper) and does not match the shape of any legitimate React Native or ECharts distribution. The `@servicetitan` scope and README references to servicetitan.atlassian.net do not correspond to a build pattern ServiceTitan uses for its React Native libraries, and are consistent with a scope-hijack or malicious release. Fetching an alternate runtime and using it to execute an obfuscated bundle at install time gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine before any consumer code runs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
